messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Possible to use parameter values from optimization as initial values for sampling within rstan?
parts: On Tuesday, January 5, 2016 at 10:20:07 PM UTC-5, Charles Driver wrote:
Is there any straightforward way to do this? I don't find the documentation regarding the structure for initial values particularly clear

Not really. You would have to unflatten the parameters. In other words you need a list with one element named hypercorrchol that is a 5x5 matrix rather than a named vector of length 25.

However, if the problem is such that MCMC needs good starting values to work well, then optimizing is not the way to find them.

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Possible to use parameter values from optimization as initial values for sampling within rstan?
parts:
Optimization and sampling _answer different questions_.  Optimization
gives a _single_ MAP estimate of the parameters which might be okay 
on average in some  cases, but does not yield reasonable uncertainty 
quantifications.  Sampling, on the other hand, explores _all_ parameters
that are consistent with the data.  In all but a low-dimensional models,
the neighborhoods in parameters space that are most consistent with
the data are very far away from the mode where optimization ends.

There are lots of pathologies that could be affecting your model.  You
could have regions of parameter space that are consistent with the
data but very hard to fit (especially likely if you have hierarchical 
structure).  You could also have non-identifiabilities, in which case
the neighborhoods of consistent parameter values are very complex
and hard to explore.  In any case, starting at the optimum does 
absolutely nothing to help.

messages.subject: Re: Possible to use parameter values from optimization as initial values for sampling within rstan?
parts:
Below is some code I used to use, but it never ended up saving me any time so I’ve since gone back to using random inits. YMMV.

rng_seed = 1111
model_file = 'foo.stan'

stan_model = stan(model_file, data = data, chains = 0)

lp_fun <- function(y) {lp = log_prob(stan_model, y); return(ifelse(is.na(lp),-Inf,lp))}
gr_lp_fun <- function(y) grad_log_prob(stan_model, y)

n_each_par = sapply(stan_model@par_dims,function(x)ifelse(length(x)==0,1,prod(x)))
n_each_par = n_each_par[-length(n_each_par)]
n_pars = sum(n_each_par)

initf = function(){
    lp__ = -Inf
    while(is.infinite(lp__)){
        init = runif(n_pars,-1,1)
        lp__ = lp_fun(init)
    }
    constrain_pars(stan_model,init)
} 

message("Finding finite inits.")
optim_init = unconstrain_pars(stan_model,initf())

message('Optimizing.')
set.seed(rng_seed)

ptm = proc.time()
o = optim(optim_init,lp_fun,gr=gr_lp_fun,method='BFGS',
    control=list(fnscale=-1,maxit=100000,reltol=.Machine$double.eps), hessian=TRUE)
message(sprintf('Optimizing took %s minutes.',round((proc.time() - ptm)[3]/60),1))

initf_optim = function()constrain_pars(stan_model,o$par)

# then use init=initf_optim in the stan call
